memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'Anyone who takes the life of a human being is to be put to death.
Anyone who takes the life of someone's animal must make restitution -
life for life'" - Lev 24:17-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice the sharp distinction God draws. Kill a man, and the penalty is
the man's own life. Kill someone's animal, and you pay for it. Animals
mattered — real restitution was required — but a human being was never
merely property to be compensated.

Why the difference? Genesis gives the reason: human beings are made in
the image of God (Gen 9:6). To destroy a person is to strike at
something that bears God's own likeness.

Dear friend, this conviction is desperately needed in every generation.
Whenever a society begins to treat some category of human life as
disposable — the unborn, the elderly, the disabled, the poor, the
prisoner, the person of another community — it has drifted from this
truth.

And the drift begins in ordinary hearts, not in legislation. Jesus
traced murder back to contempt, warning about the anger that calls a
brother worthless (Matt 5:21-22). John writes that anyone who hates a
brother or sister is a murderer at heart (1 John 3:15).

That should sober all of us. Most of us will never take a life. Most of
us have, at some point, treated a person as though they did not matter.

Ask God today to give you His view of the people you find easiest to
dismiss.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Whose life or dignity do I quietly treat as less valuable?
2. Where does contempt hide in my heart?
3. How can I honour the image of God in someone this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, every person I meet bears Your image. Forgive my contempt, and
teach me to treat each life as precious to You. Amen.
